title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the motivic Galois group (1965), here on Frobenius eigenvalues. Q' is the maximal totally real subfield of Q̄, so Q'(i) is the maximal CM subfield of Q̄, the union of all CM fields. Q'(i) contains every sqrt(-d) for d>0, since sqrt(d) is in Q'. The setting is a set M of algebraic numbers, the eigenvalues of Frobenius acting on a motive (or the characters of a torus). Fix q in Q^{*+}.

(1) A condition on M (left unstated on the page, presumably 'Weil-type') is reformulated in two ways. First: every λ in M lies in Q'(i)* (or some power does), and for each λ there is an integer i with λλ̄ = q^i. Grothendieck notes that i is determined by λ and calls it j*(λ), the weight. The condition then reads |λ| = q^{j*(λ)/2} for all λ in M.

(2) Corollary (garbled). Suppose λ is in Q̄ and λ_α λ̄_α = λλ̄ is the same rational number for every conjugate λ_α. Then the condition does not depend on the embedding Q̄ ⊂ C, and λ (or a power λ^n) lies in Q'(i). This is the standard fact that complex conjugation induces the embedding-independent involution λ ↦ q^i/λ on Q(λ). Hence Q(λ) is totally real or CM.

(3) Proposition. For λ in Q̄* and q in Q^{*+}, the following are equivalent.
(i) There is an integer i with |λ_α| = q^{i/2}, i.e. λ_α λ̄_α = q^i, for every conjugate. That is, λ is a Weil q-number of weight i.
(ii) λ (first draft: some power λ^n) lies in Q'(i), and λλ̄ = q^i for some integer i.
(iii) There is a linear algebraic group G over Q, with G_m --d--> G --ε--> G_m, Ker ε compact (anisotropic over R) and d presumably central, and an element f in G(Q) with ε(f) = q, such that λ is an eigenvalue of f in some finite-dimensional representation. Equivalently, λ is the image of f under a character of the diagonalizable part.
(iv) There is a commutative 'Riemann algebra' A over Q with an element f satisfying f f' = q^i. Here A is a commutative Q-algebra with positive (Rosati-type) involution ', and there is a homomorphism A → Q̄ sending f to λ.

Marginal notes.
- A real such λ satisfies λ^2 = q^i, so λ = ±(q^{1/2})^i: the trivial case.
- The weaker property 'all conjugates have the same absolute value' does not force λ into Q'(i). Example: λ = p^{1/4}. Its conjugates ±p^{1/4} and ±i p^{1/4} all have modulus p^{1/4}, yet Q(p^{1/4}) is neither totally real nor CM, because it has a conjugate field generated by sqrt(-sqrt p). The point is that λλ̄ = sqrt p is not rational.

Purpose: to characterise abstractly the possible Frobenius eigenvalues of polarised motives over F_q, in terms of motivic-Galois-type groups with compact 'Ker ε'. The polarisation is encoded as compactness, the weight by d.
errors: The first version of the condition asks only that λ^r lie in Q'(i). In fact λ itself lies in a CM or totally real field once λλ̄ = q^i holds in every embedding. Grothendieck seems to correct this in the second (ii), which reads 'λ ∈ Q'(i)'.
The Corollary is incomplete and crossed out in places; its hypothesis and conclusion are not clearly stated.

In (iii) the relation between d and ε (ε∘d = t^k) and the centrality of d are not stated, but they are needed for eigenvalues to have absolute value q^{i/2} with i the weight. The formula 'ε f(λ)=λ^?' is illegible.
The NB example p^{1/4} is not a Weil q-number for any rational q (|λ|^2 = sqrt p). It only shows that equal absolute values alone are insufficient; it does not show failure of the proposition.

ideas.what: Weil q-numbers: λλ̄ = q^i in every complex embedding implies Q(λ) is totally real or CM, and the weight i is determined by λ
ideas.modern_name: Weil q-numbers of weight i; Q(λ) is CM or totally real
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil; standard in Honda–Tate theory (Honda 1968, Tate 1968)

ideas.what: The maximal CM field described as Q^{tr}(i)
ideas.modern_name: maximal CM subfield Q^{cm} of Q̄
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; used by Serre, Langlands–Rapoport, Milne

ideas.what: Characterisation of Weil numbers as eigenvalues of rational elements f of algebraic groups G with weight cocharacter d: G_m→G, multiplier ε: G→G_m, Ker ε compact and ε(f)=q
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius elements in polarised (Tannakian) motivic Galois groups; Weil-number torus P / pseudo-motivic groupoid; Serre's compactness property of motivic Galois groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne–Milne (1982), Langlands–Rapoport (1987), Milne (1994), Serre (1994)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra's thesis (Catégories tannakiennes, 1972)

ideas.what: Characterisation via commutative Q-algebras with positive involution (f f' = q^i), the abstract form of Frobenius in the endomorphism algebra of a polarised abelian variety or motive
ideas.modern_name: Rosati-positive involution / Riemann form; Frobenius in End^0 with Rosati condition (Weil's proof of RH for abelian varieties)

missed.claim: This 1965 draft states an equivalence between three conditions: λ is a Weil q-number; λ is an eigenvalue of a rational element of an algebraic group with 'Ker ε compact' and ε(f)=q; λ is the image of an element f with ff'=q^i in a commutative algebra with positive involution. It anticipates the group-theoretic characterisation of Frobenius in polarised motivic Galois groups (Saavedra, Deligne–Milne, Langlands–Rapoport, Milne's Weil-number groups) by years. It is mainly historical evidence of priority rather than a new result.
missed.quote: ∃ des gr. G sur Q, et un élément f de G(Q), G_m →d G →ε G_m ... avec Ker ε compact ... ε(f)=q ... (iv) Il existe une algèbre de Riemann commutative ... appliquant f dans λ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck already linked the polarisation/positivity (compactness of Ker ε) to the Weil-number characterisation of Frobenius inside the motivic Galois group in 1965. This is relevant to crediting the origin of the Weil-number group formalism.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (Weil numbers lie in CM fields; Frobenius in a polarised motivic Galois group) is standard today. The early, explicit group-theoretic formulation with compact kernel of the multiplier is a notable historical detail. Its content was later developed and credited to others (Saavedra, Deligne–Milne, Langlands–Rapoport, Milne, Serre).
transcription_corrections: First line: 'Q' = clôture tot. réelle de Q', i.e. the maximal totally real subfield of Q̄.
'j*(λ)' is the weight of λ (the integer i); 'est même entièrement déterminé' rather than 'est même entier[?] déterminé'.
In the first condition: 'λ^r ∈ Q'(i)^*', with r = some positive power, a crossed-out first draft.
In (iii): 'G_m --d--> G --ε--> G_m' with 'Ker ε compact'; 'λ est une valeur propre de f'.
'λ = W-limite' is probably 'λ = W-linéaire' or similar; uncertain.
Margin: the example is 'λ = p^{1/4}' and the conjugate field is 'Q(sqrt(-p^{1/2}))'; the note says 'pas ⊂ Q'(i)'.
